subject: Cognitive Science
title: How We See Color
description: A quick, practical guide to How We See Color.

hook.text: A red apple isn't red. It absorbs every wavelength except red, which it bounces back to your eyes.

buildup.text: Three types of cone cells in your retina respond to short (blue), medium (green), and long (red) wavelengths.

discovery.text: Color is a mix ratio. Yellow isn't a wavelength between red and green—it's your brain blending both signals.

twist.text: Colors that don't exist on the spectrum—like magenta—are invented by your brain. No single wavelength makes magenta.

climax.text: Color vision is a compression algorithm. The brain reduces millions of wavelength combos into a manageable handful.

punchline.text: Color isn't in the world—it's in your brain.

quiz.question: How many types of cone cells do humans have?
